tool_words: You can ask the engine yourself, with the tools: the position after any moves you give it (who stands better, its best lines, what each move does) and what attacks a square. Ask it for what the messages above do not show -- what comes after the end of a line, a move they propose, whose piece a move takes, whether a square is safe -- before you answer, and say only what it returns.

function.name: analyse
function.description: Stockfish on the position reached by playing `moves` from the board now (or from before the last move): whose move it is, who stands better, the engine's best lines with what each move does, and what hangs, is pinned or can be taken there. When moves are given, also how the first one rates against the engine's best. For what the messages do not already show: what comes after the end of a line, a move the player proposes, what a move would allow.

moves.description: Moves in standard notation, in order and for both sides, played from the position `start` names (the board now by default) -- never the game's earlier moves; empty for that position itself.

start.description: now (the default): the board as it stands; before_last_move: the position the last move was played from

function.name: square
function.description: What stands on a square, which pieces of each side attack it, and which pieces of the side to move can go there, in the position reached by playing `moves` (as for analyse): whether a piece there is defended, whether a square is safe to go to, whether a check can be blocked there.

moves.description: Moves in standard notation, in order and for both sides, played from the position `start` names (the board now by default) -- never the game's earlier moves; empty for that position itself.

start.description: now (the default): the board as it stands; before_last_move: the position the last move was played from
